land.text: the Philippine Islands, held by the United States since the 1898 cession and self-governing as the Commonwealth from 15 November 1935

predecessors.note: Cliopatria keeps the Philippines in its United States shape through 1946 and starts the Republic in 1947; the Treaty of Manila was signed on 4 July 1946 (effective 22 October 1946).

capitals.name: Manila
capitals.note: The Philippines page names Manila as the capital with the seat of government in Metro Manila; it records no move.

correction.text: the Philippine Islands from 4 July 1946, when the United States recognised independence by the Treaty of Manila

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts the Republic in 1947 and keeps the islands in the United States shape for 1946. 'The Commonwealth ended when the United States recognized Philippine independence on July 4, 1946'; the page says nothing of the borders, so the modern country is used.

343,637 km2 for 1947-2023 against the infobox 300,000 km2 including inland waters (ratio 1.15, inside the factor of two). The outline is the modern archipelago. It stops at 19.44 N and so omits the single cell of Batanes (about 250 km2); the page does not mention Batanes. The Spratly features the Philippines claims (Thitu is its largest controlled island) and Scarborough Shoal (seized by China in the 2012 standoff) are not land cells and are not drawn.
Same outline as 1947; nothing on the page changes the border in 2024.

region.text: the Philippine Islands, over which 'American sovereignty' was relinquished by the Treaty of Manila (4 July 1946); the pages name no boundary

ledger.note: 1946: the Philippines becomes independent (4 July). The Treaty of Manila relinquished 'American sovereignty over the Philippine Islands' and ended the Commonwealth; the United States kept its military bases. The page names no islands or boundary, so the region is the modern country (confidence 2).

wars.name: Communist insurgency (CPP-NPA)
belligerents: Communist Party of the Philippines - New People's Army
wars.outcome: 'The CPP-NPA has fought the government since the 1970s'; no territory changed hands on the page.
wars.note: The start year 1970 stands for 'the 1970s'. Listed for completeness; the Hukbalahap rebellion (ended under Magsaysay) and the Moro conflict (MNLF peace 1996, MILF peace 2014, Bangsamoro Organic Law under Duterte) are on the page without start years or zones.

certainty.note: Judgment: the archipelago's limits are islands and treaty lines; no page opened dates a boundary treaty. The Spratly and Scarborough claims (China, Malaysia, Taiwan and Vietnam overlap) and the old Sabah claim of President Macapagal are disputed and not drawn.

notes: Page budget (1-2) spent: the Philippines article and the Treaty of Manila. Cliopatria starts the Republic in 1947 but the state begins on 4 July 1946; its United States row still holds the islands in 1946. No border change is recorded after independence on either page. The shape omits Batanes by one cell; the Spratly features and Scarborough Shoal are outside the land grid. Presidents are named without reign years on the Philippines page (Roxas at independence; Marcos 1965, martial law 1972, ousted 1986; Aquino 1986; Arroyo from 20 January 2001; Duterte elected 2016; Marcos Jr. elected 2022), so no ruler strip is given. The Seshat id pi_phililippines_rep exists but the Seshat page was not opened.
